annotation.evidence_span: might have already sent - or enqueued for sending - frames on the stream that cannot be withdrawn
annotation.interpretation_a: The peer may have sent frames that are in-flight and will arrive at the receiver, even after the RST_STREAM is sent.
annotation.interpretation_b: The peer may have enqueued frames for sending, but not yet transmitted them, and these frames are considered 'lost' upon receipt of the RST_STREAM.
annotation.justification: The phrase 'might have already sent - or enqueued for sending' introduces ambiguity. 'Enqueued for sending' could mean frames already on the wire, or frames only buffered internally. The MUST clause only addresses *received* frames, but the ambiguity lies in whether the receiver should *expect* to receive frames that were enqueued but not sent.
annotation.missing_information: It is unclear whether 'enqueued for sending' implies frames that have been added to a transmit queue but not yet physically sent, or frames that are merely buffered for a higher-layer protocol. This distinction affects whether the receiver should expect to see those frames or not.
